text: Grind 1 notch finer; extend bloom by +10s
rationale: Sharp sourness and fast drawdown indicate under-extraction. A finer grind increases contact surface area and longer bloom guarantees complete bean degassing.

text: Grind 1 notch coarser; slightly reduce total water
rationale: Dry, heavy bitterness means late-stage over-extraction of bitter tannins. Coarsening grind and ending water pour earlier maintains sweet clarity.

text: Increase coffee dose by +1g; grind 1 notch finer
rationale: Watery mouthfeel implies low TDS (Total Dissolved Solids). A slightly tighter ratio and finer grounds build richer body and aroma.

text: Grind slightly coarser; reduce agitation & swirls
rationale: A sandpaper dry finish on the tongue is caused by fines clogging and channelling. Pour gently with fewer aggressive swirls.

text: Extend bloom +10s; increase water +15g for sweetness
rationale: A hollow middle note usually means coffee grounds weren't fully saturated during bloom or the ratio was too tight to extract soluble sugars.

text: Grind slightly finer & pour in calm steady center circles
rationale: Simultaneous sourness and dryness is a hallmark of channelling (water rushing through cracks). Pour smoothly and maintain a flat bed.

text: Grind 1 notch coarser; increase water ratio for clarity
rationale: Muddy flavors obscure origin notes. Opening up the grind and using slightly more water brings back delicate floral and fruity notes.

text: Spot on! Lock in this recipe & grind setting
rationale: High sweetness, pleasant acidity, and clean lingering finish indicate optimal extraction yield (~20%).
